# `Q-5-30` — Pandoc Path Option Not Found

> A `reference-doc` or `template` entry names a file that does not
> exist, so pandoc cannot use it. Resolved relative to the file that
> declared it (a leading `/` anchors at the project root). The
> render stops here — there is nothing sensible pandoc can produce
> without the named file.

## What this means

Formats that pass through pandoc directly — `docx`, `pptx`, and
others — can point at a custom Word/PowerPoint template or a pandoc
document template with `reference-doc` and `template`:

```yaml
format:
  docx:
    reference-doc: custom-reference.docx
```

Quarto resolves the path **relative to the file that declares
it** — a value in `_quarto.yml` resolves against the project root,
a value in a directory's `_metadata.yml` against that directory, and
a value in a document's front matter against the document's own
directory. A leading `/` always anchors at the project root,
regardless of which file declares the entry.

Unlike `css` (`Q-5-29`), a missing `reference-doc` or `template` is
**fatal**, not a warning: pandoc cannot render the document without
the file the option names, so the render stops here with a
diagnostic pointing at the offending YAML entry, rather than handing
pandoc a path it cannot open.

## Common causes

- **A typo in the path**, or a file that was moved or renamed
  without updating the `reference-doc`/`template` entry.
- **A path written relative to the wrong anchor** — for example, a
  document in `posts/2026/` declaring `reference-doc: ref.docx` for
  a file that actually lives at the project root. Write `/ref.docx`
  (or the correct relative path) instead.
- **A reference document that exists on one machine but was never
  committed to the project.**

## How to fix it

Check the path in the `reference-doc`/`template` entry against the
anchor of the file that declares it, or add the missing file. If the
template belongs to the project as a whole, declaring it once in
`_quarto.yml` (project-root-relative) is usually clearer than
repeating it per document.
